subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Drawing and equations of linear graphs

questions.q: What are the coordinates of the origin?
questions.explain: The origin is the point where the x-axis and y-axis cross, at (0, 0).

questions.q: In the point (7, -3), what is the number 7 called?
questions.explain: In (x, y) the first value is the x-coordinate, giving the horizontal position.

questions.q: In which quadrant does the point (-4, 5) lie?
questions.explain: A negative x with a positive y places the point in the second quadrant (top left).

questions.q: On which axis does the point (5, 0) lie?
questions.explain: A y-coordinate of 0 means the point sits on the x-axis.

questions.q: What is the formula for the midpoint of the segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
questions.explain: The midpoint is found by averaging the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates.

questions.q: What is the midpoint of the line segment joining (2, 3) and (6, 7)?
What is the formula for the length of the segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
questions.explain: Length comes from Pythagoras' theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences.

questions.q: What is the length of the segment joining (0, 0) and (3, 4)?
What is the formula for the gradient of the line through (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
questions.explain: Gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x.

questions.q: What is the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
What is the gradient of a horizontal line?
questions.explain: A horizontal line has no vertical change, so its gradient is 0.

questions.q: A line slopes downwards from left to right. What is the sign of its gradient?
questions.explain: A line falling from left to right has a negative gradient.

questions.q: In the equation y = mx + c, what does c represent?
questions.explain: c is the value of y where the line crosses the y-axis.

questions.q: In the equation y = mx + c, what does m represent?
questions.explain: m is the gradient (steepness) of the line.

questions.q: What kind of line does the equation y = 2 represent?
questions.explain: y = 2 means y is always 2, giving a horizontal line.

questions.q: What is the equation of a line with gradient 3 and y-intercept -2?
questions.explain: Substituting m = 3 and c = -2 into y = mx + c gives y = 3x - 2.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of points needed to draw a straight-line graph?
questions.explain: Two points determine a unique straight line, though a third is useful as a check.

questions.q: What is true about the gradients of two parallel lines?
questions.explain: Parallel lines have the same steepness, so their gradients are equal.

questions.q: What is the product of the gradients of two perpendicular lines?
questions.explain: For perpendicular lines the gradients multiply to give -1.

questions.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to a line with gradient 2?
questions.explain: The perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal, so -1/2.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) syllabus; Coordinate Geometry
